literal.prompt: К какой системе органов относится желудок?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The target entity is the human stomach; the relation asked is organ-system membership; its value is the digestive system. OpenStax identifies the stomach as an alimentary-canal organ with digestive functions. The alternative labels are grounded individually: respiratory system in OpenStax 22.1; CNS/PNS in OpenStax 13.2/13.4; and the urinary tract in NIDDK. Only the digestive-system relation matches this stomach fact.

literalGroups.literal: Желудок относится к пищеварительной системе. В нём пища перемешивается с желудочным соком и начинает активно перевариваться.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The first sentence states the target organ-system relation. The second states that food is mixed with digestive juices in the stomach and digestion begins there; OpenStax also identifies the initial digestion of proteins in the stomach.

literalGroups.literal: В желудке пища перемешивается с желудочным соком, а белки начинают расщепляться под действием соляной кислоты и пепсина.
literalGroups.primaryGround: This note adds facts beyond the prompt/key: food is mixed with gastric juice and proteins begin to break down through hydrochloric acid and pepsin. Both details are explicitly stated for the stomach.

literalGroups.literal: Дыхательная система проводит воздух и обеспечивает газообмен.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note identifies the respiratory system’s gas-exchange role and conducting zone’s air route; these are explicit functions of that system.

literalGroups.literal: Нервная система принимает, обрабатывает и передаёт сигналы.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note describes the nervous system’s signal flow: peripheral sensory pathways enter the CNS, spinal pathways integrate sensory and motor activity, and motor fibers exit toward muscles.

literalGroups.literal: Мочевыделительная система включает почки, мочеточники, мочевой пузырь и мочеиспускательный канал.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note names the urinary tract’s organs. NIDDK identifies kidneys, ureters, and bladder as urinary-tract parts, and the accompanying urinary-tract figure labels the urethra.
